analysis:
Documentation-only PR with two modified files. docs/provider/direct-mode.md changes the last-updated date and adds a sentence (head lines 50-53) saying a local GLM qualification load reads weights for its own per-file SHA-256 verification, and that this is the artifact hash with no separate weight-hash passes (GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256). docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md changes the date and adds a paragraph (head lines ~45-57) recommending macOS sysctl values for 256 GB GLM hosts: iogpu.wired_limit_mb=245760, vm.global_user_wire_limit and vm.user_wire_limit=261134011596.

No code, auth, crypto, attestation or protocol behavior changes, so there is no regression against the TB-002, TB-003 or TB-007 controls or T-041. The wired-memory guidance is availability and capacity tuning. It explicitly states it changes no admission or capacity figure, and it does not weaken the load gate or the OS reserves. A higher wired limit leaves only a 16 GiB margin for the OS, which is an operator-tuning tradeoff and not a demonstrated security flaw. The weight-verification note is a description of existing behavior. It could matter for T-012 and T-027, which concern weight substitution, if it overstated what is verified, but it describes an artifact hash without claiming a coordinator weight-hash or attestation guarantee. I could not verify against source that GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256 behaves as described. I also could not verify that the referenced GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift and the troubleshooting.md anchor exist, because neither is in the supplied evidence. These are documentation accuracy questions only. The T-041 prefix-cache text is unaffected. No threat-model update is needed.
